Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Decommission & CON tracking; NIST 800-88 & service-history indexing; key risks: Device liability; Obsolescence; Rigging damage; regulatory notes: Check device-specific FDA obligations, servicing versus remanufacturing and state licensing.; Sanitize stored patient data and verify decontamination procedures.; track ids: track_1; track_2; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; Grey-Zone Growth & Traffic Arbitrage; plays: id: con_decommissioned_medical_imaging_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Certificate-of-Need (CON) & Decommissioned Hospital Imaging-Suite Arbitrage; mechanism: Acquire or option decommissioned imaging assets where approved site capacity has value, separating equipment resale economics from nontransferable or change-of-control-sensitive CON authority.; inputs: State CON decisions and hospital closure notices; Equipment service logs and site engineering surveys; Regulatory transfer guidance and buyer commitments; workflow: 1. Identify closing imaging suites and inventory equipment, permits, and lease rights; 2. Confirm CON status, transfer restrictions, radiation licensing, and deinstallation costs; 3. Negotiate approval-contingent asset purchases with qualified operators and equipment buyers; 4. Close after regulatory clearance and document certified removal, installation, and acceptance; metrics: Net resale margin after deinstallation; Regulatory approval cycle days; Buyer acceptance rate after inspection; platform risks: failure mode: CON authority lapses or cannot transfer; trigger: Closure, relocation, or ownership change outside approved conditions; impact: Loss of site premium and stranded equipment carrying costs; detection metric: Outstanding regulatory conditions and days to permit expiry; fallback: Exit under approval contingencies or sell inspected equipment separately without representing transferable operating authority; id: chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup; track id: track_1; name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups; mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.; inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register; Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents; Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall; workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices; 2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility; 3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices; 4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim; metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery; Allowed claim value versus purchased face value; Realized return and days to distribution; platform risks: failure mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion; trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims; impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss; detection metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio; fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries; id: mca_ucc_stacking_default_restructure_brokerage; track id: track_2; name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage; mechanism: Use UCC filing changes to identify businesses that may need cash-flow review and consensual MCA restructuring, with verified obligations and disclosed compensation rather than encouraging undisclosed stacking.; inputs: Public UCC filings and termination records; Merchant-authorized contracts and cash-flow statements; Broker licensing rules and disclosed creditor compensation terms; workflow: 1. Treat UCC changes as outreach signals, not proof of default, and obtain merchant authorization; 2. Reconcile advances, liens, repayment pulls, covenants, and sustainable payment capacity; 3. Disclose dual-sided fees and conflicts; use independent counsel where representation would conflict; 4. Coordinate documented creditor-approved modifications and monitor actual payment relief; metrics: Net merchant payment relief after fees; Creditor-approved modification rate; Post-restructure missed-payment rate; platform risks: failure mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default; trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts; impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability; detection metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement; fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel; platform risks: failure mode: CON authority lapses or cannot transfer; trigger: Closure, relocation, or ownership change outside approved conditions; impact: Loss of site premium and stranded equipment carrying costs; detection metric: Outstanding regulatory conditions and days to permit expiry; fallback: Exit under approval contingencies or sell inspected equipment separately without representing transferable operating authority;
